title: Volcanic winter of 536
summary: Large volcanic eruptions in AD 536 and 540 created a dust veil that historical accounts from the Mediterranean to eastern Asia say dimmed the sun for more than a year. Tree-ring records show strong, synchronised cooling across much of the Northern Hemisphere, and the cold phase from 536 to about 660 is called the Late Antique Little Ice Age. Authors link it to famine, the Justinianic plague and political upheaval.

uncertainty.note: The dust veil is dated to AD 536 and said to last more than a year; the cooling phase runs 536 to about 660 AD. Further eruptions are given for 540 and 547. The source volcano is not located in the pages I opened.

beats.caption: A dust veil from the 536 eruption dims the sun for more than a year, according to accounts from the Mediterranean to eastern Asia.
Tree rings show unprecedented, long-lasting, synchronised cooling across most of the Northern Hemisphere.
The authors link the cold phase to the Justinianic plague, upheaval in the eastern Roman empire and political upheaval in China.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the eruption source and location. Opened pages do not locate the volcano, so the point is only a Mediterranean map anchor with 8000 km uncertainty (Mediterranean cited by Helama for the accounts; Altai and Alps for the tree rings). The Scientific Reports and Nature Geoscience papers share a parent publisher (Springer Nature); Medievalists.net is a separate publisher.
